slides.headline: An Indian fintech founder now runs the app 3 billion people use to talk to each other.
Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, was named global head of WhatsApp
slides.body: On June 22, 2026, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced Shah would succeed Will Cathcart, who had led WhatsApp since 2019 - making Shah the first Indian to lead the world's largest messaging platform, used by over 3 billion people.

slides.headline: Two startups, one national acquisition record, before this.
slides.body: Shah co-founded FreeCharge in 2010, which Snapdeal acquired in 2015 in what was then India's largest startup acquisition. He founded CRED in 2018, scaling it to 17 million members and $325 million in annual revenue. His appointment came alongside a Meta-led $900 million investment in CRED itself.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: India isn't just WhatsApp's biggest market anymore. It's now leading it.
slides.body: A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs proof that building for Indian users at scale is a credential the rest of the world takes seriously. Shah's own market experience is exactly why he's now running the platform for everyone else's, too.
